denial.label: Pre-existing disease waiting period not completed

grounds: Essential hypertension was first diagnosed on 2024-05-31, AFTER the policy start date 2024-05-03; by definition it is not a Pre-Existing Disease, so the waiting period does not apply.
letter:
Subject: Appeal against Denial of Claim ID 922fb35e-148d-9e82-a14f-bc335a5f96ec  

Claim Details:  
Patient Name – Agnes Laree Weber  
Patient ID – 922fb35e-148d-9e82-7e65-bfa05e3b3515  
Date of Claim Creation – 01 June 2024  
Policy – Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Plan Code SGH‑SILVER) – Coverage Start 03 May 2024  
Diagnosis – Essential Hypertension (onset 31 May 2024)  
Procedure – Patient referral for dental care (cardiac category)  
Total Claim Amount – INR 16,089.28  
Denial Reason – D03 – Pre‑existing disease waiting period not completed  

Grounds for Appeal:  
The policy expressly defines a Pre‑Existing Disease as a condition diagnosed within 48 months prior to the first policy start date, and states that any condition first diagnosed on or after the policy start date is NOT a Pre‑Existing Disease irrespective of chronicity [suraksha_silver_policy#5]. Since Ms. Weber’s essential hypertension was first diagnosed on 31 May 2024, after the policy start date of 03 May 2024, the condition does not fall within the definition of a Pre‑Existing Disease and the 36‑month waiting period in Clause 4.2 is therefore inapplicable [suraksha_silver_policy#11].  

Burden of Proof:  
According to the insurer’s own denial standards, the burden of proving that an exclusion or waiting period applies rests with the insurer, which must produce documentary evidence that the condition was diagnosed before the policy start date [claims_procedure_and_grievance#6]. No such pre‑policy documentation has been provided; the claim file contains only the diagnosis date of 31 May 2024, confirming that the condition arose after coverage commenced.  

Clinical Necessity:  
Essential hypertension is diagnosed when clinic blood pressure readings are ≥ 140/90 mmHg on two or more separate visits, confirmed by appropriate monitoring, and the diagnosis date is the visit at which this confirmation is made [hypertension#2]. The treating physician will attach the clinical notes confirming the diagnostic readings on 31 May 2024, establishing the medical necessity of the referral for dental care as part of the patient’s overall cardiac risk management.  

Reference to Denial Standards:  
The denial was issued under standard C3.2, which requires the insurer to substantiate any waiting‑period exclusion with evidence. As the insurer has not met this evidentiary requirement, the denial does not comply with the stipulated standards [claims_procedure_and_grievance#6].  

Specific Request:  
In view of the above facts and the insurer’s failure to meet the burden of proof, we respectfully request that Claim ID 922fb35e-148d-9e82-a14f-bc335a5f96ec be re‑processed and the amount of INR 16,089.28 be paid without further delay.  

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.  

Insurance Desk (on behalf of the treating provider)

citations.section: Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Policy Wording) > 4. Waiting Periods > 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
citations.quote:
### 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
Expenses related to a Pre-Existing Disease (as defined in Clause 2.2) are covered only after 36 months of continuous coverage from the first policy start date. This waiting period applies ONLY to conditions meeting the definition in Clause 2.2.

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C3. Standards for Denial > C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
citations.quote:
### C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
The insurer bears the burden of proving that an exclusion or waiting period applies. For a Pre-Existing Disease denial, the insurer must show documentary evidence that the condition was diagnosed or treated before the policy start date.

citations.section: Essential Hypertension — Diagnosis and Monitoring > Diagnosis
citations.quote:
## Diagnosis
Hypertension is diagnosed when clinic blood pressure is ≥ 140/90 mmHg on two or more separate visits, ideally confirmed by home or ambulatory monitoring. The diagnosis date is the visit at which it was confirmed.
